markdown_report:
Synthesis of evidence

Starting-point insights: (1) SASRec represents ordered history, but its attention alone does not establish current intent. A small recent-context correction could address broadly relevant recommendations displacing immediate matches. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin; improving candidate discrimination is therefore a reasonable hypothesis. These training diagnostics do not establish validation gains. (3) Similar embedding-similarity scores across categories weaken the case for prioritizing collapse penalties. Compatibility and satisfied needs remain unobserved.

Literature insights: (1) MSMT-LSI motivates separating recent and persistent interests, while warning that sparse histories limit temporal evidence. (2) GaGNN motivates borrowing shared transition evidence when individual histories are sparse. (3) SComGNN cautions that similarity does not establish complementarity. (4) gSASRec and Scalable-SASRec motivate testing negative coverage and objectives before expensive architectural expansion.

Framework and candidate directions

| Direction / idea | Evidence used | Intended correction | O/F/U/M/D* |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Sampled softmax with 64 uniform negatives | Training prefixes | Weak ranking separation | 2/7/4/9/2 |
| B: Gated recent/persistent pooling | Ordered history | Stale or overly broad interests | 4/7/8/6/4 |
| C: Gated recent-transition residual | Directed training transitions | Broad relevance and unsupported next purchases | 5/8/8/7/4 |

*Originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, implementation difficulty; 0–10, higher difficulty means harder.*

A: Originality + controlled adaptation, − established objective; potential + reusable baseline, − limited intent modeling; user + sharper competition, − no practical-need evidence; model + directly targets separation, − sampled margins may mislead; difficulty + small change, − masking needs care.

B: Originality + restrained fusion, − established pattern; potential + extensible timescales, − sparse evidence; user + recent and repeated interests, − compatibility unresolved; model + better context, − indirect margin effect; difficulty + simple pooling, − predictor changes required.

C: Originality + bounded transition correction, − graph fusion exists; potential + interpretable collaborative evidence, − exposure bias; user + recent intent and observed next-step evidence, − transitions cannot prove utility; model + additional discrimination, − popular successors may dominate; difficulty + sparse counts, − prefix leakage requires care.

Selected idea: C

At 0% progress, retain SASRec and add a small, nonnegative gated score from normalized directed transitions following the last three items. This explicitly targets two reported failures: broad associations outranking current intent, and specialized purchases supported only by general ecosystem similarity. Observed successors provide provisional next-step evidence, never a compatibility guarantee. The residual also targets Electronics’ weak separation tail.

Build transition counts exclusively from training histories. During training, exclude each supervised transition’s own count from its feature. Smooth sparse rows toward zero, cap residual magnitude, and initialize its gate near zero. Keep baseline training initially to isolate this change.

Compare baseline versus residual using pinned macro validation HR@10; inspect all four categories. Preserve seeds, routing, unseen-item filtering and evaluator. Update predictor serialization and diagnosis scoring together. No gains are claimed before evaluation.

idea.description: Add a bounded, learned recent-transition residual to each category’s SASRec candidate scores. Combine normalized directed successor evidence from the last three observed items with the existing sequential score.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations displacing current intent and specialized purchases lacking supporting equipment or task evidence. Recent directed transitions offer a limited, observable proxy for plausible next steps. The model diagnosis identifies weak positive–negative separation, particularly in Electronics. Neither transition evidence nor improved training margins establishes functional compatibility or validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes: Use only training interactions to construct per-category sparse transition tables. Retain top-k successors after row normalization and support shrinkage; use zero for unsupported rows. Prevent direct target leakage by subtracting the supervised transition occurrence before constructing its training feature, including adjustment of support and normalization. If cached top-k features are used, construct them after subtraction or use cross-fitted tables. For a sequence prefix h and candidate j, compute r(h,j) as a recency-weighted average of successor probabilities and score s(h,j)=SASRec(h,j)+softplus(a)*tanh(c*r(h,j)), with fixed bounded c and a initialized to produce a small residual. Apply identical feature construction at inference using full training tables. Keep the existing loss for the first controlled comparison. Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment handling with default 200. Store weights and transition tables beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer to load both. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Because the residual depends on sequence IDs, adapt the view’s feature representation to carry those IDs alongside SASRec features and ensure predict_score includes the residual; view.model must reference the actual trained module. Do not fabricate metadata categories, reviews, compatibility labels, simulator traits, or results. Evaluate only through the pinned validation protocol and select by four-category macro HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    counts = directed_adjacent_counts(training_histories[category])
    model = SASRecWithTransitionResidual(gate_initial_value='near_zero')
    for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
        for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
            base_features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            # Each valid position uses only its causal prefix.
            # Remove that occurrence's supervised edge before feature lookup.
            pos_residual = transition_features(sequence, positive, counts, leave_occurrence_out=True)
            neg_residual = transition_features(sequence, negative, counts, leave_occurrence_out=True)
            pos_scores = model.score(base_features, positive, pos_residual)
            neg_scores = model.score(base_features, negative, neg_residual)
            optimize(existing_baseline_loss(pos_scores, neg_scores))
    save_trial_artifacts(model, normalized_training_transition_tables(counts))
write_predictor_with_matching_architecture_and_transition_scoring()
# Host computes pinned validation macro HR@10; no test access.

originality.positive: A bounded recent-transition correction makes a specific, testable adaptation of shared transition modeling to the diagnosed failures.
originality.negative: Combining sequential and transition signals is established; novelty is limited to the restrained adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Offers an inexpensive and inspectable basis for studying when observed next-step evidence improves recommendation specificity.
future_potential.negative: Transitions reflect exposure and popularity and cannot identify compatibility, ownership, or whether a need is already satisfied.

code_difficulty.positive: Sparse transition lookup and a scalar gate require modest changes to SASRec and its predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal prefix alignment, removal of supervised occurrences, and matching diagnostic scoring require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequential encoder and item-scoring baseline.
limitations: Sequential attention does not itself establish practical compatibility or current purchase necessity.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI
contributions: Motivates separating preferences across temporal scales, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: The supplied summary notes weaker performance under sparse Amazon histories; pinned-benchmark gains are unverified.

related_work.title: GaGNN
contributions: Combines individual and group transition structure with sequential information, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed residual or functional compatibility on this benchmark.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: Models complementary recommendation using relevance and dissimilarity.
limitations: Its complementarity assumptions cannot be inferred directly from the available interaction histories.

related_work.title: gSASRec extended abstract
contributions: Motivates reconsidering sampled BCE calibration through generalized BCE.
limitations: Does not establish that objective changes resolve the observed user-facing failures.

related_work.title: Scalable-SASRec
contributions: Provides implementations and comparisons of alternative sampled recommendation objectives.
limitations: Objective comparisons require replication under the pinned four-category validation protocol.
